$comment: 🔁️ Language-agnostic statement of the CSS animation-scope contract. The cost of a CSS animation is the size of the style invalidation it causes, not the number of animations: an animated registered custom property declared `inherits: true` and started on the document root re-resolves the computed style of EVERY element on EVERY frame. Measured on the generation3d procedural example (ticket 2026/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END, report 📓️host-reconcile-silence-2026-09-12.md): nine such clocks on `:root` cost 112.3 s of style recalculation out of 129.0 s of main-thread task time and paced the plugin host's more-work→poll continuation at one macrotask per frame, so the example converged in 110 s instead of 12.5 s. Any implementation that reads a stylesheet must answer these cases identically.

cases.name: a document-root clock on an inherited property breaks every law
an element-scoped clock on a non-inherited property conforms
a rule that only forwards the phase into another custom property is not a paint
a nested utility resolves its pseudo-element path and `animation: none` starts no clock
a paint whose clock is missing is named even when nothing animates the root
